neighbours.label: 'give(s)' meaning to lend something an appearance or effect ('gives the face an otherworldly look'), not giving an object
fire: The brass handles give the old cabinet a surprisingly modern look.
Her freckles and wide eyes gave her face a youthful appearance.
A coat of dark varnish will give the table a richer finish.
The pale stripes on its wings give the moth a ghostly appearance.
Long shadows across the valley gave the landscape a dreamlike feel.
The heavy fringe gives her haircut a softer, rounder shape.
The tinted windows give the building an imposing, mirrored look.
Adding a little lemon zest gives the frosting a brighter flavour.
quiet: The brass dealer gave the old cabinet maker a fair price for it.
Her aunt gave her a small silver locket for her birthday.
The landlord will give the tenants a month's notice before repairs.
The museum gave the moth collection to a university in Ohio.
The farmer gave the hikers directions across the valley.
The salon gives its regular customers a discount on haircuts.
The city gave the building's owners a permit for the renovation.
Her neighbour gave the children some lemons from the tree.

notes: Card: give/gives/giving x12 in 'gives X a ... look/effect'; output promotes look, feel, appears. Near misses use give in the transfer sense.
